title: IF THE OFFERING IS A GOAT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If your offering is a goat, you are to present it before the LORD, lay your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against the sides of the altar.'" - Lev 3:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Cattle, sheep, and now goats. God completes the list.

Goats were the animal of the poorer household — hardier, cheaper, less prized than sheep. And God says: bring your goat. The instructions do not change. Present it before the LORD, lay your hand on its head, blood on the altar. Identical treatment. Identical acceptance.

Three chapters into Leviticus, a picture of God's heart has emerged that many people never associate with this book. Leviticus is usually thought of as harsh, remote, obsessed with rules. But look at what it has actually been doing. Over and over, God has widened the door: bulls, sheep, birds, flour, ovens, griddles, pans, cattle, lambs, goats. He keeps naming another option so that nobody is left standing outside thinking, there was no provision for someone like me.

That is not a God trying to keep people away. That is a God determined to be reachable.

James writes that God chose those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith (Jas 2:5). Jesus began His ministry announcing good news to the poor (Lk 4:18). This is not a New Testament innovation. It was written into Israel's worship from the start.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I believed a caricature of the Old Testament God that Scripture itself contradicts?
2. Who around me feels there is "no provision for someone like me" — and how could I show them otherwise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You have always made room for the ones the world overlooks. Help me to reflect that same welcome to others. Amen.
